about: Event mode for this atlas (deploy/apply-event-mode.mjs, deploy/refresh-event-atlas.mjs). Spec by Fable, approved by Mithun 2026-10-22, with his overrides: at most 8 eat-and-drink places per venue, nearest first; the Vivanta venue is Vivanta Goa, Panaji (renamed, Campal address); Kala Academy's picture from its Wikipedia page; the Cafeteria's sessions merged into Kala Academy, which is the venue. 23 Oct 2026: one chip at a time; See & Do (Fable's call, Mithun's yes) replaces Art & Culture with parks, views, beaches, landmarks, museums, galleries and markets in four headings, churches and temples only when the data marks them notable; Utils renamed Essentials; What's around here opens Eat & Drink. Later 23 Oct: icons on every button, and a second row of buttons for See & Do's and Essentials' sub-groups (Mithun). 30 Oct 2026 (Mithun: refresh from the website and LOKA): the team's own Food and Drink tags (Joseph's, added in LOKA on 29 Oct) show under Eat & Drink beside OpenStreetMap's; Saturday's programmes corrected to emergencefestival.in in programmes-2026-10-30.json (give it as --full-text).

merges.why: Mithun, 2026-10-22: merge the Cafeteria into Kala Academy; Kala Academy is the venue.

placeFixes.name: Kala Academy

photo.credit: Press Information Bureau, Government of India (GODL-India), via Wikimedia Commons

set.description: Goa's main cultural centre, at Campal in Panaji. The Government of Goa set it up in 1970 to promote music, dance, theatre, fine art, folk art and literature. The building is by the architect Charles Correa. (From Wikipedia.)

placeFixes.source: The lead photograph of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kala_Academy, downloaded 2026-10-22 (900 × 582). Licence GODL-India: free to use with credit to the source. Description written from the same Wikipedia page, 2026-10-25.
placeFixes.why: Mithun, 2026-10-22: the tag's picture is a drawn marker; use a suitable image from the Kala Academy Wikipedia page. Mithun, 2026-10-25: the tag described the city bus stops named Kala Academy; describe the venue from Wikipedia instead.
